AfterSideTurnStart.rationale: HappyFlower.cs:79-91 is AfterSideTurnStart -- turn_structure step 23, the LAST turn-start hook, after the hand draw -- with a `participants.Contains(Owner.Creature)` filter that restricts it to the player side. The sim's on_player_turn_started is executed-confirmed to sit in exactly that slot: `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order` prints on_block_cleared -> on_energy_reset -> on_player_turn_start -> modify_hand_draw -> on_player_turn_started, and it fires only from PlayerCombatState.start_turn (player.py:186), so the side filter is structural. The arithmetic matches exactly: `TurnsSeen = (TurnsSeen + 1) % 3` then `if (TurnsSeen == 0)` gain EnergyVar(1) (lines 83-89) vs happy_flower.py:26-29. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b07.py flower-carry): turns_seen goes 1, 2, 0 over three turns and the third turn's energy is 4 instead of 3. NOTE the mapping is NOT read off relics/base.py's hook table, which PROMPT.md bug class 11 records as wrong for the adjacent on_player_turn_start slot. Rule 7: player.py and relics/base.py are not hashed by this record.

AfterCombatEnd.rationale: HappyFlower.cs:101-105 does exactly one thing -- `base.Status = RelicStatus.Normal` -- and nothing else. It does NOT reset TurnsSeen. So this is a pure presentation reset and is waived on the same basis as ShowCounter/DisplayAmount, not as a dropped state reset. The distinction is the whole of guard N1: had it cleared TurnsSeen, the port would carry belt_buckle's live defect.

guards.what: N1: the port's docstring claims 'The game's counter persists between combats; the sim's resets each combat' -- the SECOND half is FALSE, and the port is faithful precisely because it is
guards.rationale: MECHANISM: C#'s TurnsSeen is a [SavedProperty] (HappyFlower.cs:64-77) and the only AfterCombatEnd body is a Status assignment, so the counter carries across combats for the whole run. The sim initialises turns_seen in __init__ (happy_flower.py:23) and never resets it -- and relic instances live on RunState.relics and are re-attached to each new CombatState, so it carries too. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b07.py flower-carry): one player turn in each of three consecutive combats built around the SAME relic instance gives turns_seen = 1, 2, 0, and the third combat's opening energy is 4 -- i.e. the free energy lands on the third turn SEEN, across combat boundaries, exactly as the game does. Two things follow. (a) relics/base.py:20-24's claim that 'the sim runs a single combat, so per-run counters (Girya lifts, Happy Flower's carry-over turn counter) are per-combat / constructor-injected' is stale for the same reason. (b) This is the inverse of PROMPT.md bug class 12: a docstring claim about the sim that is false, but in the direction that ACQUITS the port rather than damning it -- so a reviewer who trusts the docstring would 'fix' a correct relic into belt_buckle's shape. .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md Sweep A files happy_flower under 'reset at a TURN boundary only' (the art_of_war bucket) because on_player_turn_started writes the field unconditionally; the write is an INCREMENT, not a reset, and the trace bug class 13 asks for lands on 'no reset on either side'. Rule 7: relics/base.py, run.py and the sweeps file are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: EnergyVar(1) and DynamicVar('Turns', 3m) (HappyFlower.cs:42-46) read as BaseValue for the energy and IntValue for the modulus (lines 83, 88) vs the sim's TURNS = 3 and literal 1
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so 3 and 1 are the pinned non-ascension values, and `const int turnsThreshold = 3` (line 18) agrees with the DynamicVar. The BaseValue/IntValue asymmetry is the source idiom batch 1 recorded for big_mushroom vs bag_of_preparation, not a port error.

guards.what: N3 (DORMANT): PlayerCmd.GainEnergy's `Hook.AfterModifyingEnergyGain` companion event and its `finalAmount > 0` gate (PlayerCmd.cs:29-42) have no counterpart in the sim's EnergyCmd.gain (cmds.py:545-554)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# folds Hook.ModifyEnergyGain, then fires AfterModifyingEnergyGain over the listeners that modified it, then adds only if the result is positive; the sim folds modify_energy_gain and adds unconditionally. Two divergences: the missing companion event (the same 'no AfterModifyingXxx machinery anywhere' shape audit/records/seam/damage_pipeline.json guard G2 verdicts a gap at its own site -- one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3) and the missing positivity gate, which lets a listener that returns a negative value SUBTRACT energy where the game would do nothing. DORMANT on both halves: `grep -rn 'def modify_energy_gain' sts2_rl/ --include=*.py` finds no listener that returns a negative amount, and there is no after_modifying_energy_gain hook to implement. Concrete triggers: porting any AfterModifyingEnergyGain implementer, or any modify_energy_gain listener that can drive the amount below zero. Recorded here rather than skipped because Happy Flower is one of the sim's few unconditional energy grants, so it is the natural witness. Rule 7: PlayerCmd.cs, cmds.py and the damage_pipeline record are not hashed by this record.
